newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Site of tragedy, Guatemala soccer stadium to reopen.
newsitem.headline: Site of tragedy, Guatemala soccer stadium to reopen.

text.p: FIFA, the world soccer authority, has authorised the reopening of Guatemala City's Mateo Flores Stadium, the site of a tragedy on Oct. 16 when 78 people died because of overcrowding, officials said on Monday.

Overcrowding at one entrance of the oval-shaped stadium during a World Cup qualifying match between Guatemala and Costa Rica sent a crushing wave of fans cascading down the stands toward the field. Most of the dead suffocated and others were crushed to death.
The game was postponed and matches at the stadium were suspended pending construction changes.

"The Organisation Commission for World Cup France '98, which belongs to FIFA, has informed us by fax that the suspension has been lifed," Ramiro Guerra, president of the Guatemalan events committee for the Guatemalan Football Federation, told Reuters.

"In the note they say that they are very satisfied with the changes in construction that have improved the security of the stadium, and for that the authorisation of any type of activity has been given immediately."

To comply with FIFA recommendations, stadium authorities developed a new system to prevent counterfeit tickets, added emergency exits and built new retaining walls, among other measures, officials said.

On the night of the October tragedy, 55,000 people packed a stadium built to hold 29,700, an official report said. One narrow entrance at street level was jammed with gate-crashers, sending people tumbling toward the dug-out field below.
The IV Cup of Nations, a tournament of Central American soccer teams, will be held at the stadium on Wednesday and Thursday. Some 800 security guards and police officers will work the event.
Top international soccer officials and Central American presidents were expected to arrive in Guatemala for the inauguration of the tournament.
